title: SourceReliabilityScore.v1
description: A deterministic reliability score over a SourceCandidate — the multi-factor assessment reconciliation reads to decide which source wins. It carries the authority_rank that makes the precedence checkable (source-of-law > agency FAQ) plus the per-factor signals (officialness, freshness, stability, machine_readability, contradiction_rate, availability, parse_stability, historical_accuracy). It is a derived signal, not a fact — served_as_truth is pinned [false]. Same candidate + same factors → same score, every run. Deterministic when scored_at is injected.

score_id.description: content-addressed over (candidate_id, factors); version in metadata, never in the id

authority_rank.description: the comparative authority used by reconciliation (higher outranks lower) — the load-bearing precedence signal

factors.description: the per-factor reliability signals (each 0..1 unless noted); the composite is derived from these

officialness.description: is this the source-of-record (1.0) or a restatement (lower)

freshness.description: how current the source's content is

stability.description: how rarely the source's location/structure changes

machine_readability.description: how reliably an extractor can read it (api/json > html > pdf)

contradiction_rate.description: rate of disagreement with higher-authority sources (lower is better)

parse_stability.description: how stable the extraction selectors are over time

historical_accuracy.description: track record of past verified extractions from this source

tenant_scope_ok.description: true when the source's scope matches the fact's scope (tenant_private source can't back a global fact)

composite_score.description: the derived 0..1 reliability composite (deterministic function of factors + authority_rank)

served_as_truth.description: pinned false — a reliability score ranks sources, it is never itself a served fact
